  WHY: Following the blanket prohibition could leave an orphaned session when create_trigger fails after create_session succeeds.

  PROBLEM: The new checker prompt intro says "You rename and archive no session, yourself included: never call set_session_title or archive_session" — a blanket prohibition on calling archive_session. But step 5 (pre-existing, unchanged) instructs: "If create_session is refused or fails, or create_trigger fails (then archive_session the new session first)" — requiring archive_session to clean up a newly created session whose trigger failed.
  WHY: The checker is a Sonnet session at low effort with no context beyond this prompt. Following "never call archive_session" literally, it would skip the step 5 cleanup, leaving an orphaned session when create_trigger fails after create_session succeeds.
